correctness.rationale: The return-gap coding is bijective on primitive shift orbits, and pure gap words yield only least periods a,b. The four-transition word \(A^{r-1}BAB^{s-1}\) is primitive unless \(r=s=2\), as any proper power of a four-transition cyclic word must be a square of a two-transition word. For every n>max((a+1)b,2(a+b)), the unique representative \(1\le r\le b\) with \(ar\equiv n\pmod b\) yields \(s\ge2\); either \(s\ge a+1\) and two distinct positive representations exist, or \(2\le s\le a\), \(r\ge2\), \((r,s)\ne(2,2)\), giving two distinct primitive necklaces. At the endpoint \(n=(a+1)b\) exactly one primitive mixed necklace \(A^bB\) occurs; the only alternate dominating endpoint is \((a,b)=(2,3)\), \(n=10\), with only \(AABB\) primitive. No unproved algebra or infinite computer enumeration is used. The actual standalone Python program passed 18094 zeta/necklace exact comparisons, 6120 sharp-threshold finite instances, and 192 independent cyclic-word enumerations. These are diagnostics; the general proof is analytical.

originality.rationale: The assessed result is the exact last length with fewer than two distinct primitive shift orbits in the coprime two-gap family, not the already known S-gap zeta function, the general necklace enumeration, or the period-existence spectrum. The full examined de Jong Theorem 3.19 treats the support of positive primitive orbit counts only. Dastjerdi and Jangjoo Corollary 2.3 supplies a generating function from which the orbit counts can be derived in principle, but does not give the all-parameter sharp multiplicity-two cutoff or identify its exceptional pair. The short but nontrivial two-versus-four-transition argument and sharp endpoint classification establish the optimal cutoff. No exact equivalent was found in the targeted record searches or inspected relevant primary results. Residual historical priority risk is acknowledged; this is not an exhaustive novelty certificate.
residual_risks: A historical result in run-length-limited coding, renewal-system multiplicity theory, or weighted primitive necklaces could already state the same last-singleton conductor under different language.
The known full zeta series is stronger as coefficient data; priority hinges on whether the sharp all-parameter inequality was previously extracted, not on the novelty of coefficient computation.
The earlier S-gap topology paper arxiv:1108.3242 was not fully inspected; its abstract gives no indication of this invariant, but that limited comparison is not a whole-document noncoverage finding.

value.rationale: The object is the simplest nontrivial finite S-gap shift with two return lengths, and the invariant is the natural first primitive-orbit multiplicity threshold, motivated by the difference between support-only period spectra (de Jong) and orbit-count constraints in Krieger embedding. Unlike a table of a few numerical instances, the result is a sharp complete two-parameter conductor, detects an exceptional pair, and characterizes the final one-orbit obstruction by structural run and modular arguments. It does not claim an embedding theorem, a more-than-two-gap classification, or novel zeta coefficients; these limits are explicit.
